messages.subject: mcmc::chains' get_samples method
parts:
In mcmc::chains, we have the following get_samples, which merged the samples for a parameter from all 
chains including warm up samples.  I do not think we need such a function.  Instead, we could have 

get_kept_samples(size_t n, std::vector<double>& samples), 

which merges the samples for all the chains assuming samples after warming up are good. 

719  get_samples(size_t n,
720  std::vector<double>& samples) {
721  validate_param_idx(n);
722  samples.resize(0);
723  samples.reserve(num_samples());
724  for (size_t k = 0; k < num_chains(); ++k)
725  samples.insert(samples.end(),
726  _samples[k][n].begin(),
727  _samples[k][n].end());
728  }



I think I could do the change if my thought is right.

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] mcmc::chains' get_samples method
parts:
On 6/26/12 11:23 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> In mcmc::chains, we have the following get_samples, which merged the samples for a parameter from all
> chains including warm up samples.

get_samples() on line 719 of chains.hpp does not merge
-- it only returns the samples for a single chain.
> I do not think we need such a function.

We were going to let users get the results by chain.

We want to implement all the user functionality, at least
to the extent possible, on the C++ side. The main motivation
is to keep the code size on the client (R) side down so
that it's easier to port to Python and Matlab and whatever
else people might want.

> Instead, we could have
> get_kept_samples(size_t n, std::vector<double>& samples),
>
> which merges the samples for all the chains assuming samples after warming up are good.

We have get_kept_samples_permuted() on line 774.
It merges across chains AND applies a permutation.
The same permutation gets saved and used for all
parameters.

There's no matching un-permuted get_kept_samples function.

This is because Andrew wanted to apply a permutation
to the returned samples after they're merged to
protect users from themselves.

If you want something from the R side that returns
the kept samples without permuting them, we can take it up
again with Andrew. (I also may have misunderstood his
intent.)
> I think I could do the change if my thought is right.

If you just need something on the C++ side, by
all means, go ahead and add it. I'm happy to take
a look at it after you do if you'd like.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] mcmc::chains' get_samples method
parts:
I'm happy to let users access the separate chains (including the warmup iterations), although I think that if we have a good suite of functions (including compact, readable traceplots) I don't think users will have much need for these.

I think users will _often_ want draws from all chains mixed together (discarding warmups).  These I would like permuted.  For example, suppose we have chains a,b,c,d and iterations 1-100.  Then I see no need to return a vector a1, a2, ..., a100, b1, b2, ..., b100, c1, ..., d100.  Instead I'd like 'em scrambled.  But we have to be consistent so that all parameters that are saved are scrambled the same way.

A

> a100, b1, b2, ..., b100, c1, ..., d100. Instead I'd like 'em scrambled. But we have to be consistent so that all

That's how the C++ side works now. We only
have the permuted return of the mixed chains (and
it applies a consistent permutation so that the
parameters from an iteration always have the same
index).

There's not a return of the single ordered chain.

- Bob
